**Finding: missing (high severity) — no termination for convenience**

Section 9 grants termination only for material breach (9.1), insolvency (9.2), and Vendor security/SLA/law/IP failures (9.3). Section 9.4 is absent entirely, and a document-wide search confirms no convenience right exists for either party. Since Section 8.1 locks Customer into a three-year term, the lack of any Customer convenience right triggers the rule's missing-behaviour test.

On the positive side, Vendor has no convenience right either, so no deletion was needed — the edit is purely additive and one-sided in our favour.

**Redline (validated, ok:true):** new Section 9.4 inserted after 9.3 giving Customer a 30 days' notice convenience right (whole or partial, Agreement or Order Form), without penalty or Fee acceleration, with prepaid-Fee refunds routed through the existing Section 10.2 mechanics, and expressly confirming Vendor has no convenience right during a term. The comment offers 60 days' notice as a fallback.
